version.changelog: Fix key endpoint (POST /v1/auth/anonymous), add tagged signup link

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent AI model-pricing helper that uses disclosed external APIs and does not show hidden execution, persistence, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: External network use is central to the skill and is disclosed through InferenceIndexer and provider endpoint URLs; users should expect model-selection queries and anonymous-key requests to reach third-party services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact declares a required inferenceindexer MCP server and documents a PyPI MCP package plus an external auto-discovery config, but it contains no bundled executable scripts or automatic installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language is somewhat broad for model and cost discussions, but it remains scoped to model/provider selection and does not instruct the agent to override user intent or safety rules.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, local credential harvesting, filesystem indexing, background workers, or destructive actions are present in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to recommend, price-check, and explain AI inference models using InferenceIndexer; its listed MCP tools, provider endpoint examples, and pricing fields all align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an agent to query a third-party model-pricing service before choosing inference models. Be aware that anonymous key creation and pricing/model queries may contact InferenceIndexer, and endpoint recommendations may direct you to external inference providers; avoid sending sensitive task details unless the selected provider constraints match your privacy needs.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The DeepInfra URL appears inside an example endpoint_config returned for a recommended provider endpoint, which is consistent with the skill's purpose of identifying inference hosts rather than evidence of hidden exfiltration.
[E1] expected: The InferenceIndexer anonymous-key POST endpoint is disclosed in a 'Getting a key' section and supports the stated MCP/API integration; it is third-party network behavior but not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language around model choice and cutting inference cost could cause extra invocations, but the scope remains about AI inference model/provider selection.
[SQP-1] expected: The 'When to call' section is broad but still domain-related; clearer negative examples would improve precision, but this does not create a material security concern on its own.
